operator_facts.fact: The Action runs on the node24 runtime with entrypoint action/dist/index.js (a prebuilt bundle, not the src/ TypeScript).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators pinning the action must ensure the referenced ref contains a committed dist bundle; only Node 24 runners are supported.

operator_facts.fact: Only two inputs matter for whether the action can start: secret-prefix is the sole required:true input; github-token is required in effect because readInputs throws if the resolved token is empty.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A caller can omit almost everything, but omitting secret-prefix (or blanking github.token) fails the step immediately.

operator_facts.fact: github-token defaults to ${{ github.token }} (the workflow's automatic GITHUB_TOKEN). Callers only need to override it for private-repo release/asset access or when the default token lacks the attestation read scope.
operator_facts.evidence: action.yml:58-61; installer.ts:295-308 (Bearer auth on download), installer.ts:206 (apiHeaders auth)
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The token authenticates GitHub release metadata, asset download, and gh attestation verify — not AWS. Private-fork or cross-repo installs need a token with contents:read; attestation verify needs the default token's read access.

operator_facts.fact: The token is masked via core.setSecret(token) before any installation work, and is passed to gh only through a GH_TOKEN env var in an isolated GH_CONFIG_DIR, with GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN/etc. stripped from the inherited environment first.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Token never appears in argv or logs; ambient GITHUB_TOKEN cannot leak into or override the gh verification environment.

operator_facts.fact: cli-version defaults to 0.1.1 (managed by release-please via the x-release-please-version marker comment) and must be an exact semver with NO leading v; ranges, 'latest', and v-prefixes are rejected.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators cannot float to latest; each action ref pins one CLI version. Overriding cli-version to a value with no matching vX.Y.Z release tag fails installation.

operator_facts.fact: mode is a closed union 'plan'|'sync' (default plan); any other value throws 'Input mode must be plan or sync'.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Default is the safe dry-run (plan). sync is the mutating mode and must be explicitly opted into.

operator_facts.fact: fail-on-drift (default 'false') is valid ONLY in plan mode; combining mode=sync with fail-on-drift=true throws 'Input fail-on-drift is valid only in plan mode'.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Drift-gating is a plan-mode concept; operators writing a sync job must not set fail-on-drift.

operator_facts.fact: Boolean inputs accept ONLY the literal strings 'true' or 'false' (after trim); anything else throws 'Input <name> must be true or false'. Applies to fail-on-drift, allow-empty, show-resource-names.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: YAML-y values like yes/on/1/TRUE are rejected — operators must use exact lowercase true/false.

operator_facts.fact: recovery-window-days, when present, must be an integer 7 through 30 (regex ^\d+$, no signs/fractions); empty means unset (CLI/AWS default applies).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Matches AWS Secrets Manager's 7–30 day recovery window; out-of-range or non-integer values fail at the action boundary before the CLI runs.

operator_facts.fact: run-timeout, operation-timeout, verification-timeout must match a positive Go duration built from explicit units (ns|us|ms|s|m|h, at least one non-zero digit); bare numbers or '0s' are rejected. Actual bound-checking is deferred to the Go CLI.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must write Go-style durations like 5m, 30s, 1h30m — not '300' or '5min'.

operator_facts.fact: source-root (default 'secrets') must be a canonical repository-relative POSIX path: no absolute paths, no backslashes, no '..' traversal, must equal its own normalized form.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Prevents pointing the tool outside the checked-out repo; Windows-style or traversal paths fail.

operator_facts.fact: revision defaults to GITHUB_SHA and repository-id defaults to GITHUB_REPOSITORY. revision is validated as a non-empty single-line opaque value; repository-id must match owner/repo shape ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: revision is the EXACT commit whose committed SOPS files are read — operators reconciling a specific historical commit override it; otherwise it is the triggering workflow SHA. repository-id is the ownership-tagging identity.

operator_facts.fact: secret-prefix and revision are OpaqueInput: non-empty, <=1024 chars, single-line, no ASCII control chars. aws-region is OptionalInput with the same rules but may be empty (then unset).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: aws-region is optional; when omitted the CLI/AWS SDK resolves region from the environment (AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION or instance metadata).

operator_facts.fact: Six runner env vars are mandatory and validated: GITHUB_WORKSPACE, RUNNER_TEMP, GITHUB_SHA, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, RUNNER_OS, RUNNER_ARCH. Missing any throws 'Runner environment <name> is required' before installation.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: These are set automatically by GitHub-hosted runners; self-hosted or container setups that unset them will fail early. GITHUB_SHA/GITHUB_REPOSITORY are only required when revision/repository-id inputs are not explicitly supplied.

operator_facts.fact: argv is built directly (no shell): fixed positional mode then flags --repository <workspace> --revision --repository-id --source-root --secret-prefix --log-format=json --report-file <tmp>. Optional value flags appended only when set; boolean flags (--allow-empty, --show-resource-names, --detailed-exit-code) appended only when true.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: No shell interpolation — inputs cannot inject shell commands. --detailed-exit-code is added only in plan mode with fail-on-drift=true, which is what enables exit code 2.

operator_facts.fact: Platform mapping supports only Linux/macOS and X64/ARM64. Asset name is sops-aws-sync_<version>_<os>_<arch> (os in {linux,darwin}, arch in {amd64,arm64}); tool-cache architecture uses x64/arm64. Windows or other arch throws.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Running on windows-latest or an unusual arch fails with a clear 'supports only Linux and macOS'/'only X64 and ARM64' message.

operator_facts.fact: Version resolution: GET releases/tags/v<version> must return matching tag_name; assets parsed; then git/ref/tags/v<version> is dereferenced (following annotated tags up to 5 levels) to a full 40-hex commit SHA. All GitHub API calls go only to api.github.com over https and bodies are size-bounded (<=1 MiB).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The release tag must exist and resolve to a commit; a moved/deleted tag or >5-level tag indirection fails. Asset URLs from the API are re-validated to be api.github.com https origins.

operator_facts.fact: Integrity chain: checksums.txt (exactly one asset) downloaded; the one matching '<64hex>  <assetName>' line gives expected sha256; binary downloaded; local sha256 recomputed and compared; then gh attestation verify enforces SLSA provenance; then binary is chmod 0755 and cached; then the CACHED copy's digest is re-verified.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Every install path (miss and hit) is checksum- AND attestation-verified before use; there is no fallback that skips verification.

operator_facts.fact: On a tool-cache HIT the cached binary is re-verified: digest check AND full gh attestation verify run again before reuse.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A poisoned cache entry cannot be trusted just because it exists; re-verification catches tampering across job runs on the same runner.

operator_facts.fact: Attestation policy (gh attestation verify) is pinned to: --repo meigma/sops-aws-sync, --signer-workflow meigma/sops-aws-sync/.github/workflows/attest.yml, --source-ref refs/tags/v<version>, --source-digest & --signer-digest = release commit, --cert-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, --deny-self-hosted-runners, --predicate-type https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1, --digest-alg sha256, --format json.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The Action only trusts binaries provably built by the project's own attest.yml on GitHub-hosted runners for that exact tag+commit. Forked releases or re-signed binaries will not pass.

operator_facts.fact: Before verifying, the Action probes the installed gh: 'gh --version' must match 'gh version N.N.N' and 'gh attestation verify --help' must advertise all 10 required policy flags, else it fails closed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: gh must be present on the runner (it is on GitHub-hosted runners) and new enough to support attestation policy flags; an old/missing gh fails with 'A compatible GitHub CLI is required'.

operator_facts.fact: Attestation JSON output is independently parsed: it must be a non-empty array with at least one statement whose predicateType is the SLSA v1 URL AND whose subject digest.sha256 equals the expected binary digest.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Even a zero-exit gh call is not trusted blindly; the digest binding is re-checked in-process.

operator_facts.fact: Any non-ActionError thrown during install is normalized to the generic 'Exact CLI installation or verification failed'; the temp download dir and gh config dir are always removed in finally blocks.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Verification failures surface as a failed step with a safe generic message; underlying network/infra details are intentionally hidden.

operator_facts.fact: The CLI is executed silently with command echo disabled; only CLI stdout lines (JSON logs) are forwarded via core.info. If the CLI writes ANYTHING to stderr, a single fixed warning 'sops-aws-sync wrote a diagnostic to stderr' is emitted (stderr content itself is never logged).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators debugging must rely on the JSON stdout log lines and the redacted report; raw stderr is suppressed to prevent secret leakage.

operator_facts.fact: Outputs published: status, cli-version, git-revision, create-count, update-count, restore-count, scheduled-delete-count, unchanged-count, conflict-count, verification-status, redacted-report-path. All are sourced only from the schema-validated redacted report (except redacted-report-path).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: These are the only machine-consumable results; downstream steps read secret NAMES/values nowhere here — only counts and statuses.

operator_facts.fact: The step summary renders two tables (Status/CLI version/Git revision/Verification and the six counts) built only from the validated report — no secret names or values.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Safe to leave summaries visible; they contain aggregate metadata only.

operator_facts.fact: The report file is written under a fresh mkdtemp dir in RUNNER_TEMP chmod 0700; the report is size-bounded (<=64 KiB), must be JSON with EXACTLY the keys schema_version/tool_version/git_revision/status/counts/verification/duration_ms, schema must equal 'sops-aws-sync/report/v1', counts must be exactly six non-negative integers, and string fields reject control chars / >1024 chars.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Unexpected/extra report fields or a schema bump fail the step; this is a hard compatibility contract between the pinned CLI version and the action version.

operator_facts.fact: Exit-code → outcome mapping: 0 success; 2 plan drift (only when fail-on-drift, --detailed-exit-code); 3 invalid config/desired state; 4 ownership/observed conflict; 5 apply/observation failed; 6 verification failed/inconclusive; 130 interrupted; anything else 'unsupported exit status'. Each nonzero code sets the step failed with a fixed message.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators gate on these: exit 2 means drift detected (the fail-on-drift use case), exit 4 means an ownership boundary was hit, exit 6 means secrets did not converge.

operator_facts.fact: validateExit cross-checks the numeric exit code against report.status and throws 'CLI exit status and redacted report disagree' on mismatch (e.g., exit 0 with status not converged/drift, or exit 2 without status=drift+plan+fail-on-drift).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A version-skew between the pinned CLI and the action (different exit/status semantics) manifests as this disagreement error rather than silent wrong results.

operator_facts.fact: allow-empty (default false) forwards --allow-empty to authorize an empty desired snapshot to schedule managed deletions; without it an empty snapshot is presumably rejected by the CLI.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A critical safety gate: accidentally emptying the secrets dir will not mass-schedule deletions unless the operator explicitly opts in with allow-empty=true.

operator_facts.fact: show-resource-names (default false) forwards --show-resource-names to explicitly allow resource identifiers in CLI logs; default keeps names redacted.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: By default secret/resource names are kept out of logs; operators must opt in to see them, trading debuggability for confidentiality.

operator_facts.fact: The Action provides NO AWS authentication of its own. argv carries only --aws-region; the CLI relies on the ambient AWS SDK credential chain the caller must establish before this step (e.g., aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials OIDC).
operator_facts.evidence: command.ts:5-52 (no AWS creds in argv); action.yml:31-33 (aws-region only)
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators MUST run an AWS credential step earlier in the job; missing/insufficient credentials surface as CLI runtime failures (exit 4/5), not as action input errors.

operator_facts.fact: All thrown user-facing errors are ActionError with pre-sanitized messages; any other error becomes 'sops-aws-sync Action execution failed'. The whole run is wrapped so any failure calls io.setFailed with a safe message.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: No stack traces, tokens, or secret values ever reach the step's failure message; operators get only curated diagnostics.

mental_model: The Action is a thin, verification-heavy wrapper: it (1) parses/validates inputs, (2) installs a checksum- and SLSA-attestation-verified pinned CLI binary, (3) builds a shell-free argv, (4) runs the CLI, (5) reads a strictly-schema'd redacted report and maps exit codes to step outcomes. It performs NO AWS work itself.

The trust root is the project's own release: a binary is used only if its sha256 matches checksums.txt AND gh attestation verify proves it was built by meigma/sops-aws-sync/.github/workflows/attest.yml for the exact tag+commit on a GitHub-hosted runner (SLSA provenance v1). This holds on both cache miss and cache hit.

Version is fully pinned and immutable: cli-version is exact semver (default tracked by release-please), resolved to tag v<version> and its underlying commit; there is no 'latest' and no range floating.

plan is the safe default (dry run); sync is the only mutating mode. Drift-gating (fail-on-drift → exit 2) exists only in plan mode. Empty-desired-state deletions require an explicit allow-empty opt-in.

Secrets confidentiality is enforced structurally: token masked and passed only via isolated GH_CONFIG_DIR env; CLI stderr is never logged (only a fixed warning); outputs/summary derive solely from a redacted, key-exact report; resource names are hidden unless show-resource-names is set.
AWS authentication is the caller's responsibility — the Action only forwards an optional --aws-region and depends on the ambient AWS SDK credential chain established by a prior step.

Exit code and report status are a two-part contract that must agree; disagreement (a sign of CLI/action version skew) is itself a hard failure. The report schema is exact-key-matched, so a schema bump between CLI and action versions fails closed.
Every failure path yields a curated, non-sensitive message (ActionError) or a single generic fallback; infrastructure/network/secret detail never reaches logs or step failure text.

operator_facts.fact: Desired state is derived exclusively from SOPS JSON blobs committed at one exact Git revision; the working tree is never consulted. BuildDesiredSnapshot loads the snapshot via a SourceRepository at the resolved revision, decrypts each blob, and maps its path to an AWS name.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must commit and push secret changes before a sync will act on them; uncommitted or unpushed edits are invisible.

operator_facts.fact: Only files ending in '.sops.json' are eligible desired documents; the AWS secret name is SecretPrefix + '/' + (relative-path-minus-'.sops.json'). E.g. root=secrets, prefix=myapp, file secrets/db/prod.sops.json => myapp/db/prod.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Renaming or moving a source file changes the derived secret name (and its source identity), which the tool sees as delete-old + create-new, not a rename.

operator_facts.fact: AWS secret names are validated: non-empty, <=512 bytes, characters restricted to [A-Za-z0-9] plus /_+=.@- . Any other rune is rejected.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Source file/dir names (after prefixing) must yield only these characters or desired-state construction fails with OutcomeInvalid.

operator_facts.fact: Canonical secret value must be non-empty and <=65536 bytes of canonical (RFC 8785) JSON. Update/no-op decisions compare the desired canonical JSON bytes byte-for-byte against the live AWS SecretString.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A secret already in AWS whose stored payload is not byte-identical canonical JSON will be rewritten (Update) even if semantically equal; payloads over 64KiB are rejected.

operator_facts.fact: Revision must be a full 40-character hex Git SHA-1 (lowercased); short SHAs, tags, or branch names are not accepted at the domain layer.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The caller must resolve any commit-ish to a full 40-char SHA before it reaches the domain; otherwise construction fails.

operator_facts.fact: Ownership is asserted with three reserved AWS tags: 'sops-aws-sync:managed-by'='sops-aws-sync', 'sops-aws-sync:scope'=<scope digest>, 'sops-aws-sync:source'=<source path SHA-256>. A secret is owned only if managed-by AND scope both match exactly.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The tool will never mutate a secret lacking these exact tags; manually retagging or a scope change orphans previously-managed secrets.

operator_facts.fact: Scope identity is a versioned SHA-256 over 'sops-aws-sync:scope:v1' + RepositoryID + cleaned SourceRoot + prefix (trailing slash trimmed). Changing any of the three inputs produces a new scope that owns nothing previously created.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Renaming the repo ID, moving the source root, or changing the secret prefix silently abandons all prior secrets (they become foreign) and re-creates them under the new scope.

operator_facts.fact: Source identity is SHA-256 of the cleaned repository-relative source path. Classification treats a name-matching secret whose source tag differs from the desired document's source as ObservedForeign (conflict class 'source').
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Two different source files that would map to the same AWS name collide as a foreign conflict rather than overwriting each other.

operator_facts.fact: The plan is the union of desired names and discovered scope members. Per desired name: Missing=>Create; OwnedActiveString matching value=>unchanged else Update; OwnedActiveBinary/Unknown/WithoutCurrent=>Update; OwnedScheduled=>Restore; Foreign/Conflict/Invalid=>conflict.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: An owned secret currently holding binary or lacking an AWSCURRENT version is always rewritten to the desired string; drift in value triggers Update.

operator_facts.fact: Discovered scope members NOT in desired state: OwnedActive*=>ScheduleDeletion; OwnedScheduled=>counted unchanged; Foreign/Conflict/Invalid=>conflict; Missing=>ignored. This is how removing a source file leads to deletion.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Deleting or renaming a committed SOPS file causes the previously-created secret to be scheduled for deletion on the next sync.

operator_facts.fact: Deletion is never immediate: it is AWS scheduled deletion with an explicit RecoveryWindowDays passed straight to ScheduleDeletion. An owned secret already scheduled is left as-is (unchanged).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Deleted secrets remain recoverable for the configured window; re-adding the source file within that window produces a Restore rather than a fresh create.

operator_facts.fact: Restore is a two-step lifecycle: Restore (cancel scheduled deletion) then an update-only follow-up cycle writes the desired value. After restore the secret is owned-active but may still hold a stale value, so applyRestoreFollowUp performs at most ONE additional update cycle for the restored names.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Restoring a secret to its committed value can take two internal cycles; a restore that cannot complete its single follow-up update fails as OutcomeVerification.

operator_facts.fact: Operations execute in a fixed deterministic phase order: Restore(1), Create(2), Update(3), ScheduleDeletion(4), Unchanged(5); ties broken by ascending name. Conflicts are also sorted by class.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Restores and creates always precede deletions within one apply, so operators can reason about ordering deterministically across identical inputs.

operator_facts.fact: Every operation carries a secret-safe expected-state fingerprint = SHA-256 over name|kind|source|SHA-256(payload)|version|conflictClass. Immediately before mutating, the live state is re-observed and CheckPrecondition compares fingerprints: match=>Apply, achieved=>Succeeded, conflict kind=>Conflict, otherwise=>Replan.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Concurrent external changes between plan and apply are detected and cause a safe rebuild or conflict rather than clobbering; raw secret values never appear in fingerprints or logs.

operator_facts.fact: Idempotency tokens (128-bit random hex, 32 chars) are generated ONLY for Create and Update. Restore and ScheduleDeletion use no token. An ambiguous (uncertain) mutation result triggers re-observation; only Create/Update may be safely retried with the SAME token, while ambiguous Restore/ScheduleDeletion become inconclusive => OutcomeApplyFailed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A network hiccup during a create/update is retried idempotently; the same during a delete/restore fails safe rather than risking a double action.

operator_facts.fact: A harmless precondition mismatch during apply (TransitionSucceeded or TransitionReplan) returns errPlanChanged, causing at most ONE full plan rebuild (maximumPlanRebuilds=1). Exceeding one rebuild yields OutcomeVerification.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The tool self-heals from a single round of benign concurrent drift; persistent churn from another writer surfaces as a verification failure rather than looping forever.

operator_facts.fact: Empty-desired-state safety gate: if the desired snapshot is empty AND the plan contains any ScheduleDeletion AND AllowEmpty is false, the run is blocked with OutcomeInvalid before any mutation.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A misconfiguration that yields zero source files cannot mass-delete an entire scope unless the operator explicitly sets AllowEmpty; deletions from a non-empty snapshot are NOT gated.

operator_facts.fact: Post-apply verification re-observes the entire scope on a 250ms poll until the plan converges (or a conflict appears), bounded by VerificationTimeout. It explicitly re-observes every applied target even if scope discovery (eventually-consistent listing) omits it.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Sync only reports success after independently confirming convergence; slow AWS list propagation is tolerated up to VerificationTimeout, after which the result is verification-inconclusive.

operator_facts.fact: Verification outcomes distinguish: converged (success), failed (plan didn't converge => OutcomeVerification), inconclusive (stabilization timeout, distinct from parent cancellation => interrupted), not-run.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: 'verification-inconclusive' means the writes likely succeeded but AWS did not stabilize in time — a retry/longer timeout is the remedy, not a re-apply from scratch.

operator_facts.fact: Scope discovery only considers list candidates whose managed-by and scope tags match exactly (IsScopeCandidate) and observes their metadata WITHOUT reading payloads (ClassifyManaged). Payloads are read only for desired names and only when metadata proves the secret owned and safe (CurrentPayloadRequired).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Discovery cannot see or delete secrets outside the exact scope, and never decrypts/reads values of scope members it is only considering for deletion — minimizing exposure.

operator_facts.fact: Safety conflicts block the whole plan (validatePlan returns OutcomeConflict). Conflict classes are: ownership, source, service-owned, rotation, replication, staging, payload, source-tag. Service-owned, rotation-enabled/in-progress, replicated, or ambiguous-staging owned secrets are refused as conflicts even though tagged as managed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The tool refuses to touch secrets with rotation, replicas, service ownership, or inconsistent staging labels; operators must resolve these in AWS before the sync can proceed.

operator_facts.fact: Discovery returning two candidates with the same name is a hard error ('scope discovery returned a duplicate name'), as is two source documents mapping to the same secret name, and duplicate desired/observed names in ValidateObservedSet.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Name collisions fail fast rather than producing nondeterministic behavior; operators must ensure source paths map to unique names.

operator_facts.fact: Convergence/idempotency guarantee: an already-converged scope yields zero operations and zero conflicts (Plan.Converged), because OwnedActiveString with a matching source and byte-equal value is classified unchanged. Re-running sync on a converged state is a no-op.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Repeated syncs are safe and cheap; the Plan command reports 'converged' vs 'drift' without mutating, suitable for CI drift detection.

operator_facts.fact: Resource names are redacted from logs by default: operations log an ordinal 'resource-NNNN' unless ShowResourceNames is explicitly true.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Secret names (potentially sensitive) stay out of logs unless the operator opts in; enable ShowResourceNames only in trusted log sinks.

operator_facts.fact: The machine report is schema 'sops-aws-sync/report/v1' with fields: schema_version, tool_version, git_revision, status, counts{create,update,restore,schedule_delete,unchanged,conflicts}, verification, duration_ms. Status values observed: converged, drift, conflict, invalid, apply-failed, observation-failed, interrupted, verification-failed, verification-inconclusive.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: This JSON is the stable contract for CI parsing; 'drift' only comes from the Plan command, and counts are secret-free totals.

operator_facts.fact: Preflight/observation failures map to distinct statuses: cancellation => interrupted; unavailable/unknown observation => 'observation-failed'; invalid config/desired => invalid; conflict => conflict. AWS errors are logged only as normalized metadata (operation, code, fault, request_id), never raw text.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators diagnose failures by status class plus the safe AWS error code/request-id in logs; raw secret or error text is never emitted.

mental_model: Truth lives in Git, not AWS: desired state is the set of *.sops.json files at one exact 40-char commit; AWS is reconciled toward it. Nothing acts on uncommitted changes.

A secret is 'yours' only if it carries all three reserved tags with managed-by=sops-aws-sync AND a scope digest matching (RepositoryID, SourceRoot, SecretPrefix). Change any scope input and every prior secret becomes 'foreign' and is abandoned/recreated.
Secret name and source identity are both derived deterministically from the file's repository-relative path. Moving/renaming a file is delete+create, never a rename.

The plan is the union of desired names and tag-discovered scope members: present-in-git => create/update/restore; absent-from-git-but-in-scope => scheduled deletion; wrong tags/rotation/replica/service-owned/bad-staging => a blocking conflict.
Deletion is soft (AWS recovery window) and reversible: re-adding a file within the window restores rather than recreates.
Every mutation is guarded by a re-observed, secret-safe fingerprint precondition; concurrent external drift causes a safe single rebuild or a conflict, never a blind overwrite.
Only Create/Update are idempotently retryable (client tokens); ambiguous Restore/ScheduleDeletion fail safe as inconclusive rather than risk a double action.
Empty desired state is treated as dangerous: it cannot trigger deletions without explicit AllowEmpty. Deletions from a non-empty snapshot are not gated.

Success is only claimed after independent scope-wide verification converges within VerificationTimeout; timeout is 'inconclusive' (writes probably landed), distinct from an actual verification failure.
Determinism: identical inputs always produce the same ordered plan (phase order Restore, Create, Update, ScheduleDeletion; name tiebreak) and re-running a converged scope is a pure no-op.
Secrets never leak: values are compared as canonical-JSON bytes and hashed into fingerprints; logs show ordinals by default and only normalized AWS error metadata.
configuration_surface: ReconcileInput.RepositoryID (string) — stable ownership identity; part of scope digest
ReconcileInput.SourceRoot (string) — repository-relative dir selecting SOPS JSON docs; part of scope digest; '.' means repo root
ReconcileInput.SecretPrefix (string) — AWS name prefix and ownership boundary; trailing '/' trimmed; part of scope digest
ReconcileInput.VerificationTimeout (time.Duration) — bounds post-apply stabilization polling (250ms poll interval, fixed)
ReconcileInput.AllowEmpty (bool, default false) — authorizes scheduled deletions when the desired snapshot is empty
ReconcileInput.RecoveryWindowDays (int32) — explicit AWS Secrets Manager recovery window passed to ScheduleDeletion
ReconcileInput.ShowResourceNames (bool, default false) — enables real secret names in logs instead of resource-NNNN ordinals
DesiredInput.Revision (string) — commit-ish resolved by the source adapter; domain requires a full 40-char hex SHA
DesiredInput.SourceRoot / DesiredInput.SecretPrefix — mirror the reconcile scope for desired-state construction
Constant maximumSecretNameSize=512 bytes (name length cap)
Constant maximumSecretValueSize=65536 bytes (canonical JSON payload cap)
Constant maximumPlanRebuilds=1 (harmless-drift rebuild budget)
Constant verificationPollInterval=250ms (fixed verification/restore poll cadence)
Constant ReportSchemaVersion='sops-aws-sync/report/v1'
Reserved tag keys/values (fixed, not operator-tunable): sops-aws-sync:managed-by, sops-aws-sync:scope, sops-aws-sync:source, value sops-aws-sync
Scope hash version prefix 'sops-aws-sync:scope:v1' (fixed; a future bump would re-scope everything)
failure_modes: OutcomeInvalid (status 'invalid'): unresolvable config or desired-state — bad/short revision, name with unsupported char, empty or >64KiB payload, two docs mapping to one name, or empty snapshot with pending deletions and AllowEmpty=false.

OutcomeConflict (status 'conflict'): a scope member is foreign (missing/wrong tags), source-tag mismatch, service-owned, rotation-enabled/in-progress, replicated, has an invalid/ambiguous AWSCURRENT staging, or a malformed source tag. Any single conflict blocks the entire plan before mutation.

OutcomeApplyFailed (status 'apply-failed'): a mutation failed or returned an unresolvable ambiguous result — includes ambiguous Restore/ScheduleDeletion (inconclusive), same-token retry still failing, or a token-generation failure.

OutcomeVerification failed (status 'verification-failed', verification 'failed'): more than one harmless rebuild was needed, a restore follow-up plan contained unexpected operations, or scope-wide verification never converged.

Verification inconclusive (status 'verification-inconclusive', verification 'inconclusive'): writes likely succeeded but AWS did not stabilize within VerificationTimeout — remedy is longer timeout/retry, not re-apply.
OutcomeInterrupted (status 'interrupted'): context cancellation/deadline during preflight, apply, or verification.
Observation-failed (preflight status 'observation-failed'): discovery or direct observation of the desired/scope union failed before planning.
Hard internal errors (surfaced as invalid/apply-failed): scope discovery returned duplicate names, or duplicate desired/observed names violating ValidateObservedSet.

Silent-scope-abandonment (not an error, but operationally severe): changing RepositoryID, SourceRoot, or SecretPrefix re-scopes ownership so prior secrets appear foreign and a fresh set is created under the new scope.

operator_facts.fact: The committed Git tree at an exact commit is the sole desired state; AWS Secrets Manager is the observed state. One selected Git file maps to exactly one AWS secret.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Core mental model: operators change AWS state by committing SOPS files, not by editing AWS directly. The working tree, index, and untracked files are never authoritative (DESIGN.md:142-144).

operator_facts.fact: The reconciliation engine is pure business logic that imports no AWS, go-git, SOPS, Cobra, Viper, logging, filesystem, or GitHub Actions APIs, and returns a deterministic plan from typed desired/observed inputs.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Explains why plans are deterministic and auditable without AWS/Git access, and why the plan output is stable and testable — a guarantee operators can rely on for reviewability.

operator_facts.fact: Only files ending in .sops.json under the source root are selected, recursively; a matching entry must be a regular Git blob — a symlink, submodule, or other mode fails desired-state construction. Directories and non-matching entries are skipped.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must name secret files with the .sops.json suffix and cannot use symlinks/submodules as secret sources; V1 is JSON-only (no YAML/dotenv/INI/binary, DESIGN.md:66-67).

operator_facts.fact: File-to-secret name mapping: strip source-root prefix, strip .sops.json suffix, preserve remaining path components and case, join to the required secret prefix with '/'. Example: source root 'secrets' + prefix '/acme/payments' + 'secrets/production/database.sops.json' => '/acme/payments/production/database'.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Deterministic, predictable naming. The mapper never replaces unsupported characters (would risk collisions); invalid names or duplicate mappings fail before any AWS mutation (DESIGN.md:172-174).

operator_facts.fact: Ownership requires three reserved tags to match exactly: 'sops-aws-sync:managed-by' = 'sops-aws-sync', 'sops-aws-sync:scope' = a stable SHA-256 scope identifier, and 'sops-aws-sync:source' = SHA-256 digest of the repo-relative source path. The scope id is derived from repository identity, source root, AWS secret prefix, and a versioned derivation label.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Defines the ownership boundary. Two different configurations cannot silently share ownership. Operators must understand a secret is only 'managed' if all three tags are valid — otherwise it is foreign and untouched.

operator_facts.fact: A same-name secret outside scope, with missing/invalid ownership tags, or with a different source digest is a CONFLICT; the tool never adopts it implicitly. Non-reserved tags on a managed secret are preserved.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Fail-closed guarantee: the tool will never overwrite, retag, restore, or delete an unowned same-name secret. Operators must manually resolve conflicts (e.g., by tagging or renaming) before sync can proceed.

operator_facts.fact: An empty desired set is rejected ONLY when the resulting plan would schedule one or more managed secrets for deletion; --allow-empty authorizes those new deletions. If every managed secret is already scheduled for deletion, a later run converges without the flag.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Guards against accidentally deleting all secrets when the source directory is empty/misconfigured. The flag is only needed for the transition run, not steady state.

operator_facts.fact: SOPS decryption uses decrypt.DataWithFormat(bytes, formats.Json) on committed blob bytes, NOT decrypt.File (which would read the working tree and violate the commit snapshot). The SOPS binding verifies the document MAC before returning plaintext.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Integrity guarantee: tampered ciphertext fails the MAC check. The commit-snapshot contract is preserved even for decryption.

operator_facts.fact: The tool accepts SOPS partial-encryption policies and does NOT claim every JSON leaf was encrypted. Repository paths, JSON keys, SOPS metadata, and explicitly unencrypted fields remain visible in Git and are governed by repository policy.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Critical security caveat: operators must NOT assume all data in a .sops.json file is confidential. Unencrypted fields and keys are plaintext in Git.

operator_facts.fact: Plaintext contract: exactly one JSON value, top-level must be a JSON object; rejects duplicate object keys, trailing data, invalid numbers, invalid UTF-8; rejects encrypted blobs above --max-encrypted-bytes and canonical values above Secrets Manager's 65,536-byte limit; encodes with RFC 8785 JCS.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must ensure decrypted documents are single top-level JSON objects under 64KiB canonical. JCS canonicalization means formatting-only differences converge once and never cause churn (DESIGN.md:228-232).

operator_facts.fact: Canonical JCS bytes are the exact SecretString stored in AWS. The reconciler compares canonical desired bytes with the raw current SecretString and does not write a new version when identical (no-op).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: No-op comparison prevents unnecessary secret versions — operationally important because Secrets Manager retains versions and warns against sustained high-frequency updates.

operator_facts.fact: Decrypted bytes exist in process memory only: never written to disk, never in a report, command line, env var, or log. Because Go strings/slices and the AWS SDK do not permit reliable zeroization, the tool makes NO memory-erasure guarantee.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Threat-model boundary operators must internalize: secrets are protected from egress channels but not guaranteed scrubbed from memory during process lifetime.

operator_facts.fact: The pure planner returns exactly one decision per identity per a fixed matrix: present/absent=create; present/owned-active-equal=unchanged; present/owned-active-different-or-binary-or-missing-AWSCURRENT=update; present/owned-scheduled-deletion=restore; absent/owned-active=schedule-deletion; absent/owned-scheduled-deletion=unchanged; present/foreign-scope-or-source=conflict; unsupported service/rotation/replica/staging=conflict; malformed observed=conflict.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The complete, deterministic decision table operators reason from. Any conflict prevents ALL mutation in that cycle (DESIGN.md:318-320).

operator_facts.fact: Restore is a separate reconciliation cycle because Secrets Manager cannot read a scheduled secret's value. The first plan restores; the next observation decides update or unchanged. Exactly ONE follow-up apply cycle is permitted for successfully restored names; further restores or unrelated new operations indicate concurrent drift and fail the run.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Restoring a deleted-scheduled secret takes two cycles; if drift keeps changing state, the run fails safely rather than looping.

operator_facts.fact: Operation phase order is fixed: 1) restore, 2) create, 3) update, 4) schedule-deletion. Deletions are last so a failure cannot remove access before available creates/updates complete.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Safety ordering guarantee: a partial failure never leaves you with deletions applied but creates/updates missing.

operator_facts.fact: Every executable operation carries a typed expected-state fingerprint. Immediately before each mutation the app re-observes the name and calls a pure transition function returning exactly one of: apply, succeeded, retry-same-token (only while resolving one ambiguous write), replan (harmless drift), conflict (ownership/safety changed), or inconclusive.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Precondition/CAS-like safety: the tool never blindly repeats a mutation. Explains ambiguous-write recovery behavior and why runs can end 'inconclusive'.

operator_facts.fact: A plan is CONVERGED only when it has zero executable operations AND zero conflicts. 'unchanged' is summary metadata, not an executable operation. The planner evaluates the union of desired names and observed scope members; it does not enumerate the unbounded absent/absent namespace.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Definition of success operators verify against. Secrets outside the scope tags are invisible to planning.

operator_facts.fact: AWS credentials come exclusively from the standard SDK v2 chain via config.LoadDefaultConfig (env vars, web identity, shared files/profiles, container roles, instance roles). Static credentials are NEVER accepted by application configuration. Only optional Region and profile overrides are exposed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators authenticate the tool the same way as any AWS SDK client; there is no flag/input for access keys or session tokens. Missing credentials/Region is an actionable config error.

operator_facts.fact: Observation paginates ListSecrets with IncludePlannedDeletion=true using reserved tag filters as an optimization only, then calls DescribeSecret directly for every desired name (including names not returned by the list) and merges results. GetSecretValue is called for AWSCURRENT only when the secret is active and its value is needed for planning/verification.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The union of list + direct describe detects same-name foreign secrets before mutation. Tag filters are prefix matches, so the pure domain does exact membership classification (DESIGN.md:196-198).

operator_facts.fact: Secrets Manager is eventually consistent; AWS documents ListSecrets can lag up to five minutes. Direct DescribeSecret/GetSecretValue are fresher for known names but cannot reveal an unknown scope member omitted from a stale list. Success is NOT a claim of a globally strongly consistent AWS snapshot.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must run single-writer workflows; the tool relies on workflow-level single-writer controls plus concurrency groups because AWS gives no cross-secret transaction/CAS (DESIGN.md:456-458,838-842).

operator_facts.fact: Mutation mapping: create=CreateSecret with canonical SecretString + ownership tags; update=PutSecretValue; restore=RestoreSecret; schedule-deletion=DeleteSecret with explicit recovery window. ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery is NEVER set and not exposed. Recovery window defaults to 30 days, must be within AWS's 7-30 day range.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: No permanent/force deletion exists in V1. Scheduling deletion makes the secret unavailable immediately but recoverable within the window. TagResource is used on create only; no separate retag operation (DESIGN.md:828-831).

operator_facts.fact: Each create/update gets a fresh cryptographically random ClientRequestToken per logical write, retained only across SDK attempts and domain-approved ambiguous-outcome recovery. A later run or newly observed precondition creates a new token, so a stale token never blocks repair when the same commit/value must become AWSCURRENT again after drift. Tokens are never logged.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Explains why external drift is repaired even with an unchanged Git commit — a design-critical correctness property (a stale token would otherwise block re-write).

operator_facts.fact: Preflight CONFLICTS: non-empty OwningService, enabled/in-progress rotation, unsupported replica state, ambiguous AWSCURRENT staging, or deleting a replicated primary secret. Rotation, service ownership, and replication management are outside V1.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The tool refuses to manage secrets with rotation, service ownership, or replication configured; operators must not point it at such secrets.

operator_facts.fact: The AWS SDK standard retryer is authoritative for retryable network/timeout/throttling/service failures. Config can adjust bounded max attempts and max backoff; infinite retries are invalid. Every AWS call gets the run context plus a shorter operation deadline; cancellation stops further attempts.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Retry behavior is bounded and tunable via --aws-max-attempts / --aws-max-backoff / --operation-timeout. Cancellation is honored between attempts.

operator_facts.fact: A timeout or connection loss AFTER a mutating request is an ambiguous outcome: the app re-observes that exact name and passes operation/precondition/token/new evidence to the pure transition function. It never blindly repeats an ambiguous mutation outside SDK request-level retry.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Explains resilience to lost responses without risk of double-writes; ties to the ClientRequestToken idempotency mechanism.

operator_facts.fact: Completed operations are NOT rolled back. On partial failure the CLI stops scheduling new operations, reports non-sensitive completion counts, exits nonzero; a later run resumes from observed state. There is no atomic multi-secret transaction and no rollback of completed AWS calls.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must treat sync as resumable-forward, not transactional. Re-running after a partial failure is the recovery path.

operator_facts.fact: The SOPS decrypt package does not accept context.Context; internally data-key recovery uses context.Background(). The CLI runs one decrypt at a time in a single-use worker; cancellation is TERMINAL — the adapter returns an interruption, the composition root emits one fixed safe event, and the process exits WITHOUT waiting for the worker. Process termination ends the provider request; no cooperative cancellation inside SOPS is claimed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: During SOPS decryption, --run-timeout / SIGINT terminates the process rather than cleanly cancelling the in-flight KMS/provider call. No AWS mutation begins until every decrypt succeeds (DESIGN.md:528).

operator_facts.fact: SOPS's global loggers can include provider identifiers such as a KMS ARN; the composition root suppresses SOPS library logging by default and emits its own redacted start/success/failure events.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Guards against KMS ARNs and provider identifiers leaking via SOPS's own logging into operator log streams.

operator_facts.fact: CLI command family is exactly: plan, sync, version. 'plan' does discovery + returns a redacted plan with NO AWS mutation; --detailed-exit-code makes detected drift return exit 2. 'sync' does full reconcile+verify, is non-interactive with no confirmation flag, returns 0 only after an empty verified plan. 'version'/--version report release/commit/build date without loading config or AWS.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The only mutating command is 'sync'; its explicit name is the safety gate (no --yes). 'plan' is always safe/read-only. 'version' needs no credentials.

operator_facts.fact: Configuration precedence: flags > SOPS_AWS_SYNC_* environment > optional config file > defaults. Malformed files, unknown config keys, invalid durations, and invalid enum values fail before side effects. Env names replace hyphens/dots with underscores (e.g., SOPS_AWS_SYNC_SECRET_PREFIX, SOPS_AWS_SYNC_OPERATION_TIMEOUT).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The complete precedence and env-naming rule operators need. Unknown keys are rejected, not ignored — typos fail loudly. AWS's own env vars stay owned by the AWS SDK; Viper does not copy credentials (DESIGN.md:605-607).

operator_facts.fact: Required config with no default: --repository-id (stable ownership identity; Action supplies owner/repo) and --secret-prefix (AWS name prefix + ownership boundary). Defaults: --repository='.', --revision='HEAD', --source-root='secrets', --max-encrypted-bytes='8MiB', --allow-empty=false, --recovery-window-days=30, --run-timeout='10m', --operation-timeout='30s', --verification-timeout='2m', --log-level='info', --log-format='json', --show-resource-names=false.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The full knob inventory with defaults. --repository-id and --secret-prefix must always be supplied. --config is an optional YAML tool-config path (desired secret documents remain JSON-only).

operator_facts.fact: Stream contract: production operational logs to stdout; Cobra usage and emergency logging-init failure to stderr; plaintext and encrypted secret data go NOWHERE; stable machine results go to --report-file (not mixed into the log stream). The Action always selects --log-format=json.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators parse stdout for JSON logs and --report-file for machine results; stderr is only for usage/init failures. This overrides the TS template's default stream convention.

operator_facts.fact: The report contains schema version, tool version, Git revision, status, operation counts, conflict count, verification result, and durations. It OMITS by default: secret values, JSON keys, ciphertext, credentials, KMS identifiers, secret names, and source paths.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Reports are safe to archive/share by default; resource names/paths appear only with --show-resource-names.

operator_facts.fact: Stable exit codes: 0=plan completed or sync verified convergence; 2=plan --detailed-exit-code found executable drift; 3=invalid input/config/desired state; 4=ownership or observed-state conflict; 5=apply failed or unknown/partial result; 6=verification failed or inconclusive; 130=interrupted by SIGINT/SIGTERM/parent cancellation.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: These are a stable compatibility surface for scripting/CI. Each code maps to a distinct operator remediation path.

operator_facts.fact: Default logs include only counts, durations, operation kinds, retry decisions, safe AWS error codes, and request IDs. They must NOT include decrypted/encrypted contents, JSON keys/values, credentials/tokens, secret version payloads, unsanitized SDK/SOPS errors, KMS ciphertext/data keys/provider identifiers, or secret names/paths unless --show-resource-names is set. Debug logging does not weaken the plaintext prohibition.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Even at --log-level=debug secrets never appear. Without --show-resource-names a run-local ordinal like 'resource-0001' correlates events but supports no offline lookup (DESIGN.md:658-661).

operator_facts.fact: AWS log fields are limited to operation, safe error code, fault class, request ID, retryability, and redacted resource reference. Raw request/response bodies and unsanitized error strings are forbidden. Error classification uses modeled Secrets Manager errors, smithy.OperationError, smithy.APIError, and the AWS response request ID.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators debug AWS failures via safe error codes + request IDs (correlatable with AWS support), not raw error text.

operator_facts.fact: The Action is a thin adapter performing exactly five responsibilities: parse inputs to immutable typed config; resolve+install one checksum- and provenance-verified CLI release; construct an explicit argument array; invoke the binary directly via @actions/exec without a shell; read the redacted report and publish safe outputs + step summary. It does NOT inspect Git, decrypt SOPS, call AWS, classify AWS errors, retry, or diff state.
operator_facts.evidence_note: Design intent for the Action boundary
operator_facts.operator_relevance: All reconciliation logic lives in Go; the Action cannot be a source of behavioral surprise. No arbitrary args input is accepted (DESIGN.md:689).

operator_facts.fact: @actions/exec runs with silent:true and ignoreReturnCode:true so command echo and thrown exit errors cannot expose secret-prefix, source-root, or repository-id. The binary is invoked by absolute path with GITHUB_WORKSPACE as working directory and --repository value; user input is never interpolated into a shell.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Even non-secret config values are kept out of Action logs by default; the Action handles the numeric exit status explicitly.

mental_model: Source of truth: the SOPS-encrypted files committed at an exact Git commit are the ONLY desired state. AWS is observed, never authoritative. You change AWS by committing files, not by editing secrets directly (DESIGN.md:10-13,142-144).

Ownership is tag-based and exact: a secret is 'managed' only when managed-by, scope (a SHA-256 derived from repo identity + source root + secret prefix + versioned label), and a valid source-path digest all match. Anything else is foreign and never touched (DESIGN.md:184-203).

Fail-closed by default: any conflict (foreign same-name, malformed state, rotation/service/replica/staging constraint) blocks ALL mutation in that cycle. The tool never adopts, overwrites, or deletes unowned secrets (DESIGN.md:200-203,318-320).

Convergence definition: success = the fully paginated observed scope plus every desired and affected name has zero executable operations and zero conflicts. This is NOT a claim of a globally strongly consistent AWS snapshot (DESIGN.md:316-322,449-458).

Determinism: the same desired+observed states always produce the same sorted, immutable plan, auditable without AWS or Git, because reconciliation is pure domain logic with no infrastructure imports (DESIGN.md:15-18,324-333).
Safety ordering: operations always apply restore -> create -> update -> schedule-deletion, so a partial failure never removes access before creates/updates land (DESIGN.md:351-359).

Idempotency without double-writes: fresh per-write ClientRequestTokens plus precondition re-observation and a pure transition function (apply/succeeded/retry-same-token/replan/conflict/inconclusive) mean ambiguous writes are resolved by re-observation, never blind repetition; no-op comparison avoids needless versions (DESIGN.md:334-349,476-485).

Resumable-forward, not transactional: there is no cross-secret transaction, no rollback of completed calls. Partial failures stop scheduling new work, exit nonzero, and a later run resumes from observed state (DESIGN.md:513-515,72-74).

Single-writer assumption: AWS gives no cross-secret CAS/transaction, so correctness depends on caller-enforced single-writer workflows (concurrency groups) and running only from protected default-branch merges — never PR code with credentials (DESIGN.md:456-458,835-842).

Secret confidentiality is partial and non-guaranteed: only SOPS-encrypted fields are confidential (keys, paths, metadata, unencrypted leaves are plaintext in Git); decrypted bytes live in memory only with no zeroization guarantee; secrets never reach logs/reports/CLI/env even at debug level (DESIGN.md:211-238,646-661).

Supply-chain trust: the Action runs a binary that executes with the caller's AWS identity, so checksum + SLSA provenance verification against a strict identity/ref/digest/issuer policy is mandatory and fail-closed for both downloads and cache hits (DESIGN.md:729-764).

Interruption during SOPS decrypt is terminal, not cooperative: the process exits rather than cleanly cancelling an in-flight provider (KMS) call, because SOPS's stable decrypt API is not context-aware. No AWS mutation begins until all decrypts succeed (DESIGN.md:517-535).

The design references a signer workflow '.github/workflows/attest.yml' and consumer ref 'meigma/sops-aws-sync@<ref>' (DESIGN.md:667,754); whether these exact paths/names shipped must be confirmed against the repo.

The 'terminal process boundary defined in Section 12' for SOPS calls (DESIGN.md:57,592) implies run-timeout enforcement mid-decrypt kills the process; exact exit-code behavior for a run-timeout (vs SIGINT) during decrypt is not explicitly mapped in the exit-code table.

operator_facts.fact: Git content is read via go-git's PlainOpen against a local repository path plus ResolveRevision on an operator-supplied revision string, then CommitObject/Tree — this reads from the committed object database of a local clone, not the working tree/index, so uncommitted or staged-but-uncommitted changes are never seen.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must commit and push changes before running the tool; a local dirty working tree has no effect. The tool needs a full local clone available at repositoryPath (e.g. actions/checkout in CI) with the target revision fetched.

operator_facts.fact: The resolved commit hash is re-normalized into domain.Revision and returned as the exact snapshot revision — the tool re-derives and reports the literal commit SHA it operated against (via ResolveRevision + commit.Hash.String()), not merely echoing the caller's ref/branch input.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators can pass a branch name, tag, or short SHA as `revision` and the tool resolves it once to an exact SHA at start; this exact SHA becomes the recorded provenance (used later for the source ownership tag), so results are reproducible per-commit even if the branch moves during a long run.

operator_facts.fact: Only files matching the exact suffix `.sops.json` are treated as documents; discovery walks the tree recursively (TreeWalker with recurse=true) under an optional `sourceRoot` subtree.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must name their encrypted secret files with a literal `.sops.json` suffix; other SOPS-encrypted extensions (`.enc.json`, `.sops.yaml`, etc.) are silently invisible to the tool — not an error, just not selected.

operator_facts.fact: Any tree entry whose name matches the suffix but whose git file mode is not `filemode.Regular` (e.g., a symlink or submodule/gitlink pointing at `.sops.json`) causes a hard error aborting the whole load, rather than being skipped.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A symlinked or submodule-based `.sops.json` path in the committed tree fails the run entirely; operators must ensure these are regular committed blobs.

operator_facts.fact: Each candidate blob's size is checked against a caller-supplied `maxEncryptedBytes` limit (must be positive, enforced in NewReader) before reading; oversized blobs error out the whole Load rather than being skipped.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: There is a configurable maximum encrypted-input size; hitting it fails the run (fail-closed), acting as a defensive/DoS guard against huge or maliciously large committed blobs.

operator_facts.fact: Context cancellation is polled at the start of Load, once per tree-walk iteration (per file), and is not polled inside file reads themselves.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A run can be cancelled between files but a single very large file read is not interruptible mid-read (bounded in practice by maxEncryptedBytes).

operator_facts.fact: Document path returned for downstream identity/tagging is `path.Join(sourceRoot, name)` when sourceRoot != '.', else the bare tree-relative name — this path becomes part of the committed-source identity used elsewhere (e.g., source ownership tag).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: The exact relative path (including sourceRoot prefix) is significant identity data, not just a debug label.

operator_facts.fact: SOPS decryption is delegated entirely to the upstream `github.com/getsops/sops/v3/decrypt` package's `DataWithFormat` call with format fixed to JSON (formats.Json) — no other SOPS format (YAML, ENV, INI, binary) is accepted regardless of what the underlying library could handle.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Encrypted files must be valid SOPS JSON documents; the format is hardcoded, not sniffed or configurable. Key/backend resolution (age recipients, KMS, PGP, Vault, etc.) is whatever the vendored SOPS library resolves from its own standard environment (e.g. SOPS_AGE_KEY(_FILE), AWS KMS ARNs in the file's metadata, GPG keyring) — this adapter does not add or restrict key sources itself; it is a thin pass-through to sops's own MAC/key verification, which enforces the SOPS MAC (integrity of all values) as part of `decrypt.DataWithFormat`.

operator_facts.fact: On any decryption failure (bad ciphertext, MAC mismatch, missing/inaccessible key) the adapter discards the underlying SOPS error text and returns a fixed, non-descriptive error string 'SOPS JSON decryption failed'.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators cannot distinguish, from this tool's own error output, whether decryption failed due to wrong/missing keys, corrupted ciphertext, tampered MAC, or KMS/age backend unavailability — all collapse to the same message (deliberate redaction, presumably to avoid leaking key material/paths in errors).

operator_facts.fact: After decryption, plaintext is validated to be valid UTF-8, parsed with json.Decoder using UseNumber (preserves number precision), required to be a top-level JSON object, checked for duplicate member names at every nesting level (consumeObject tracks `seen` keys and errors on duplicates), and then transformed via RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (jcs.Transform) before being wrapped in domain.SecretValue.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Decrypted plaintext that is not a JSON object (e.g., a bare array/scalar/string secret), contains duplicate keys, or isn't valid UTF-8 is rejected even though SOPS decryption itself succeeded — this is a strict content contract beyond what SOPS enforces, and downstream secret values are always exact canonical JSON of an object.

operator_facts.fact: Decryption runs in a background goroutine and the caller races it against ctx.Done(); on context cancellation/timeout the function returns immediately, but the spawned goroutine is not cancelled/killed — it keeps running to completion in the background (result channel is buffered size 1 so it won't leak/block).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A decryption timeout does not stop the underlying SOPS call (e.g. a hung KMS network call); the goroutine leaks until SOPS itself returns, though the caller has already moved on and the buffered channel prevents that leak from blocking anything forever.

operator_facts.fact: Input size is checked against `maxEncryptedBytes` (constructor-enforced positive int) before decryption, and the encrypted bytes are defensively copied (`isolated := append([]byte(nil), encrypted...)`) before being handed to the background goroutine.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Same class of defensive size limit as the git reader; also documents that the caller's original slice can be mutated/reused safely since the decrypter takes its own copy.

operator_facts.fact: AWS Secrets Manager operations used: ListSecrets (paginated via NextToken, filtered server-side by tag key `sops-aws-sync:managed-by` = value `sops-aws-sync`, with IncludePlannedDeletion=true), DescribeSecret, GetSecretValue (with explicit VersionId + VersionStage=AWSCURRENT pinning), CreateSecret (with ClientRequestToken for idempotency and 3 reserved tags), PutSecretValue (ClientRequestToken + VersionStages=[AWSCURRENT]), RestoreSecret, DeleteSecret (RecoveryWindowInDays, never ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Implied minimum IAM permissions: secretsmanager:ListSecrets, DescribeSecret, GetSecretValue, CreateSecret, PutSecretValue, RestoreSecret, DeleteSecret. No TagResource/UntagResource call exists — tags are only ever set at CreateSecret time, never updated afterward, so secretsmanager:TagResource is NOT required by current code and existing secrets' tags cannot be repaired by this tool.

operator_facts.fact: Every AWS SDK call is wrapped in its own `context.WithTimeout(ctx, operationTimeout)` derived from the adapter's configured `operationTimeout` (constructor-enforced positive duration) — a fresh timeout per call, not one shared deadline for a whole Discover/Observe loop.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Discover's pagination loop applies operationTimeout to each ListSecrets page call individually, so a large tag-scoped inventory needing many pages is not bounded by a single timeout — only each page fetch is bounded.

operator_facts.fact: Retry/throttling behavior is entirely delegated to the AWS SDK's standard retryer; LoadOptions.MaxAttempts and MaxBackoff optionally override the SDK's standard retryer only when at least one is > 0 (via awsconfig.WithRetryer + retry.NewStandard) — otherwise the SDK's built-in default retry policy applies untouched.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: There is no custom application-level backoff/retry logic for throttling (e.g. AWS's own exponential backoff with jitter is what applies); operators tune retries only via MaxAttempts/MaxBackoff config knobs, otherwise defaults apply silently.

operator_facts.fact: Load() requires AWS Region to be non-empty after LoadDefaultConfig (explicit check `awsConfiguration.Region == ""`) and eagerly calls `Credentials.Retrieve(ctx)` to fail fast on missing/invalid credentials before returning a working adapter.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators get an early, explicit failure if AWS_REGION/config profile region is unset or if the credential chain (env vars, shared config, IMDS/IRSA, SSO, etc.) can't produce credentials — rather than deferring to the first API call.

operator_facts.fact: All configuration/credential load failures are wrapped in `loadError`, whose `Error()` returns one of exactly two fixed strings ('AWS configuration is invalid' or 'AWS credential loading failed') and never echoes the underlying SDK/provider error text, though the original cause is retained via Unwrap() for internal/log inspection.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: CLI-surfaced top-level messages for AWS setup problems are deliberately generic; distinguishing configuration vs. credential problems is possible via the `ConfigurationFailure()` bool but the two failure classes look identical to an operator reading only the message text unless the caller inspects the typed error.

operator_facts.fact: Eventual-consistency / staging handling: Observe() only fetches the current secret payload when `domain.CurrentPayloadRequired` determines it's needed, and cross-checks the fetched VersionId/VersionStages against the previously observed DescribeSecret metadata; if GetSecretValue's actual version/stage doesn't match what DescribeSecret reported, `StagingValid` is set false rather than trusting the fetched payload.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: This is the tool's explicit defense against AWS Secrets Manager's read-after-write / multi-version eventual consistency: if DescribeSecret and GetSecretValue disagree (e.g., a version moved between calls, or more than one AWSCURRENT version exists — evidenced when `len(currentVersions) != 1`), the adapter marks the observation as unreliable (StagingValid=false / no CurrentVersion set) so the reconciliation layer can react (e.g. treat as drift/ambiguous rather than acting on stale data).

operator_facts.fact: `RotationInProgress` is derived from any version carrying the AWSPENDING stage label in DescribeSecret's VersionIdsToStages map; `HasReplicas` is derived from a non-empty ReplicationStatus list; `OwningService` falls back to the secret's `Type` field if `OwningService` is empty.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: These are additional signals exposed to the domain/reconciliation layer to let it decide whether to skip or flag secrets under rotation or replication, rather than blindly overwriting them.

operator_facts.fact: DescribeSecret's ResourceNotFoundException is specifically caught and translated into an empty (`Exists:false` implied by zero-value) ObservedEvidence rather than an error, distinguishing 'secret does not exist' from a genuine API failure.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A missing secret is a normal/expected state (candidate for create), not a failure path; only other API/service errors propagate as SafeError.

operator_facts.fact: `reservedTags` copies out only the three domain-reserved tag keys (managed-by, scope, source) from AWS's returned tag list, discarding any other tags the secret may carry.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Non-reserved/custom tags on a secret are invisible to this tool's decision logic entirely (neither read nor preserved/considered) — the tool reasons only about its own 3 ownership tags.

operator_facts.fact: Create() always writes exactly the three reserved tags (managed-by=sops-aws-sync, scope=<ScopeIdentity>, source=<committed source identity>) at creation time using a ClientRequestToken for idempotent retries; there is no code path that updates tags on an existing secret (no TagResource/UntagResource calls anywhere in the file).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: If reserved tags are ever removed/corrupted on an already-existing secret (e.g. by manual AWS console edits), this adapter has no mechanism to repair them post-creation — ownership tagging is create-time-only.

operator_facts.fact: All AWS-originated errors are funneled through `classifyError`, which builds a `SafeError` exposing only: a fixed 'AWS <operation> failed' message, the AWS error Code (via smithy.APIError.ErrorCode()), Fault class (client/server, via ErrorFault()), an AWS RequestID (if the error implements a ServiceRequestID() method), an `Ambiguous` bool, and a `Canceled` bool — raw AWS error message text is never retained/exposed.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators debugging AWS failures get code/fault/requestID as structured, safe fields (suitable for logs/support cases) but never the original AWS error string, which might contain ARNs or other details deemed sensitive; RequestID is the actionable value for opening an AWS support case.

operator_facts.fact: `Ambiguous` is only ever true for mutation operations (Create/Update/Restore/ScheduleDeletion — `mutation=true` passed to classifyError) and only when the failure looks like a timeout, a cancellation, or a network-level error (net.Error), never for a clean synchronous API error like ValidationException.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: This is the tool's signal for 'the write may or may not have actually applied server-side' (e.g., request timed out after AWS received it) — reconciliation/retry logic upstream should treat Ambiguous=true mutation failures specially (e.g. re-Observe before retrying) rather than blindly retrying with a new token, since ClientRequestToken idempotency only covers Create/Update (not Restore/DeleteSecret, which take no token).

operator_facts.fact: Read-only operations (list/describe/get-current) always pass `mutation=false` to classifyError, so they can never be marked Ambiguous even under timeout — only mutating calls get that ambiguity signal.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: A timed-out read simply fails; only a timed-out/canceled/network-failed write is flagged as possibly-applied.

operator_facts.fact: The logging adapter builds exactly one of two slog.Handler kinds (JSON or text) at exactly one of four accepted levels (debug/info/warn/error, case-sensitive lowercase strings); any other level or format string is a hard construction error — there is no default fallback level or format.
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Operators must pass exactly one of the 4 level strings and one of the 2 format strings (any typo/case mismatch like 'INFO' or 'Json' errors out at startup); log level and format are the only two knobs this constructor exposes.

operator_facts.fact: The logging adapter itself performs zero redaction logic — no field filtering, scrubbing, or secret-masking code exists in logger.go; it is a bare `slog.New` wrapper around the standard library JSON/Text handlers with only a minimum-level filter (`HandlerOptions{Level: minimum}`).
operator_facts.operator_relevance: Any redaction of secret values (e.g. never logging SecretString/canonical JSON contents) must be enforced by callers choosing what to pass as log fields/args — this adapter provides no safety net; nothing here prevents a caller from accidentally logging a domain.SecretValue's plaintext. Correspondingly, note that secretsmanager.SafeError and sopsdecrypt's fixed-string errors are the actual redaction mechanisms observed in this codebase (structurally preventing sensitive text from ever reaching an error/return value in the first place), rather than any logging-layer scrubbing.

mental_model: Git reading is always exact-commit, read-only, and object-database-based (via go-git PlainOpen + ResolveRevision + CommitObject + Tree) — never the working tree, index, or staged changes; the operator-facing 'revision' input can be any git-resolvable ref but is immediately pinned to one literal commit SHA for the whole run and echoed back as provenance.

Document discovery is purely suffix-based (`.sops.json`) and mode-strict (regular blobs only); a matching non-regular entry (symlink/submodule) is a hard error, not a skip — the reader is fail-closed on ambiguity, not permissive.

SOPS decryption here is a narrow JSON-only slice of the full SOPS format matrix, delegated wholesale to the upstream sops library for both cryptographic verification (MAC integrity, key resolution across whatever backends the vendored SOPS library supports — age/KMS/PGP/Vault/etc.) and decryption; this adapter adds a second, independent content contract on top (UTF-8, JSON object, no duplicate keys, RFC 8785 canonical form) that plaintext must also satisfy.

Every decryption failure — whether wrong key, corrupted ciphertext, MAC failure, or unreachable KMS — is deliberately collapsed into one fixed opaque error message; the tool treats 'why decryption failed' as sensitive and never surfaces SOPS's native diagnostic text to operators.

The AWS adapter's core invariant is ownership-scoped safety: only secrets carrying the exact reserved tag triple (managed-by=sops-aws-sync, scope=<value>, source=<value>) are ever mutated as 'owned'; Discover finds candidates by managed-by+scope tag filter server-side, Observe/ObserveManaged do direct per-name lookups, and CurrentPayloadRequired gates whether a payload fetch is even attempted — the domain layer, not this adapter, decides ownership semantics from the ReservedTags map this adapter returns.

Every AWS mutation is idempotency-aware only where the SDK itself supports it: Create/Update take a ClientRequestToken; Restore/ScheduleDeletion(Delete) do not — so retry semantics differ by operation, and the Ambiguous flag on SafeError is the signal that a mutation may have silently succeeded despite an error being returned (particularly consequential for the two token-less operations).

AWS eventual consistency is handled defensively, not assumed away: a version/stage returned by GetSecretValue is only trusted if it matches what DescribeSecret most recently reported; disagreement or multiple AWSCURRENT versions flips StagingValid to false rather than the adapter guessing which value is authoritative.

Tags are write-once-at-creation: this tool has no tag-repair/update path for existing secrets, so 'ownership tagging' as a resync/repair capability does not exist in this adapter — it exists only at Create time.

All three adapters (git, sops, aws) share a philosophy of defensive size/time bounding (maxEncryptedBytes limits, per-call context timeouts) and of returning safe/generic error surfaces that discard potentially sensitive underlying detail (raw AWS error text, raw SOPS error text, raw credential-provider detail) while preserving structured, inspectable metadata (Code/Fault/RequestID/Ambiguous/Canceled, ConfigurationFailure) for programmatic handling.

The logging package is a pure mechanism (level+format selection) with no redaction responsibility; sensitive-value safety is architecturally pushed into the other adapters' error types instead of into the logger, so 'is a secret ever logged' depends entirely on caller discipline, not this package.
